answer: Because the timing is written down against the nadir challenge, the lantern audit can replay the velvet history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. A scripted farm therefore has to pad 54 submissions and hold each identity open and idle instead of firing and forgetting, which forfeits the operator in machine time and adds nothing to the reward. That bill is paid per identity, so 156 aliases cost 341 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
